titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 38: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 38. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number ⲗⲏ (top left) is printed with a bar above and below as the frame, not as a supralinear stroke. Stroke over the first ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲟⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ only (794–807, 92 %) and over ϥ of ⲛϩⲏⲧϥ (1009–1021).

Strokes over ⲙ of ⲧⲙⲡⲥⲁⲡ (809–822), the first ⲙ of ⲙⲙⲁⲥ (981–994) and ⲙ of ⲁϫⲙ (1114–1127); the tool's 30 % figures are against merged boxes of two letters, each stroke covers about 60 % of its own letter.
A blank of about 56 px, not marked by the editors, stands before ⲧⲟⲧⲉ.
The letter after ⲧⲟⲧⲉ at the edge of the left 4× strip looked like ϯ; on the join strip (x 880–1020) it is the ⲡ of ⲡⲁϫⲉϥ, so no ϯ is read.
Line in ekthesis with an enlarged ϫ.

Strokes over ⲙ of ϩⲙ (662–675) and ⲛ of ⲛⲑⲉ (891–904).

Strokes over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲉ (688–701) and over the restored ⲙ of [ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ] (1106–1120). Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (847–868, pixel row): ⲙ 50 %, ⲛ 60 %, encoded on both.
All ϣ on the page were checked in the lower-zone sheets (ll. 1, 5, 9, 12–14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 23, 25, 30–32); none has a separate sublinear dot.
